chunks: And from him, from Sindi ibn Muhammad al-Bazzaz, from Aban ibn Uthman al-Ahmar, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl al-Hashimi, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: "The compatible one is he who is chaste and has financial means."

key_terms.الْكُفْوُ: The compatible or equal match in marriage
key_terms.عَفِيفاً: Chaste, pious, or free from moral defects

ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for marital compatibility (kafa'ah) in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In the context of Shia jurisprudence, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes that kafa'ah is not limited to lineage but fundamentally requires moral integrity (iffah) and financial capability (yasar). This definition was pivotal in the juristic debates regarding the validity of marriage when one party lacks equal status, emphasizing that practical stability and piety outweigh rigid social stratification. It serves as a primary textual basis for the principle that a woman may marry a man of lesser status provided he meets these two core conditions.
